diagram_math_checks.justification: Definition lines 37–39 put q_j at x_j and v_{i,j} at x_j+(h/2)e_i. With the left cell represented by [0,3] x [0,2.5], its pressure centre is (1.5,1.25). The next centre is (4.5,1.25), and their common vertical face x=3 carries v_{1,j}; the left face x=0 carries v_{1,j-e_1}. Top/bottom face bars at (1.5,2.5)/(1.5,0) carry v_{2,j}/v_{2,j-e_2}. The rectangular aspect ratio is schematic.

G_h maps scalar cell arrays in tilde Q_h to face arrays V_h (lines 41–47). The positive e_1 arrow points from the q_j cell toward q_{j+e_1}. Therefore the shared face label is accompanied by (G_h q)_{1,j}=(q_{j+e_1}-q_j)/h, exactly line 47, without implying a sign for arbitrary velocity values.

D_h maps V_h to Q_h (lines 45–47). The illustrated left cell has right-minus-left first-component contribution and top-minus-bottom second-component contribution. Their sum is precisely the d=2 specialization displayed below the diagram, with no missing component or reversed sign.

Lines 32–35 reduce every coordinate index modulo N and identify opposite domain faces. Remarks explicitly call this a local periodic lift and state q_{j+N e_1}=q_j. Dotted horizontal continuations mark extension rather than physical boundaries; the two labels remain valid also when N=2. No new boundary condition or distinct-index assumption is introduced.

The underlying Definition remains unchanged. Both displayed operator relations are direct specializations of line 47 and all storage positions come from lines 37–39. No proof or later argument is replaced by the illustration; no new supplier/dependency is asserted.
